facts.raw_span: A young girl initially came under care at age 4 years
developed an irregular brown-black patch on her left lateral ankle, measuring 3.6 × 3 cm
triangular hyperpigmented, asymptomatic patch consisting of confluent mottled black and brown macules and several satellite lesions
slow but progressive growth of the hyperpigmented patch, which had increased to 5.5 × 5-cm
two discrete areas of regression were noted
discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas with gray-brown structureless areas and a negative pigment network were observed
No induration was palpated except at the previous biopsy site
Shows a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction consistent with an atypical compound nevus
Shows atypical nevus with areas of dermal fibrosis
Score: -7.1 (where scores from -16.7 to -2.1 are consistent with a benign nevus)
A large, dark brown patch consisting of coalescing macules and satellite lesions
The patch shows areas of regression on the medial and left upper borders

concepts.why: The patient developed a hyperpigmented patch at a young age, which is consistent with a congenital melanocytic nevus, and histopathology showed a compound nevus with atypical features.
The patient's nevus showed atypical features on histopathology, including large nested melanocytes and dermal fibrosis, which is consistent with an atypical nevus.
The patient has a pigmented skin lesion that is consistent with a melanocytic nevus, and dermoscopy showed a typical pattern of a nevus.
The patient's nevus had a low score on gene expression testing, which is consistent with a benign nevus, and histopathology showed a compound nevus with no significant atypia.
The presence of discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue areas on dermoscopy explains the uncovered fact.

rationales.F02: The presence of a brown-black patch on the ankle is more typical of congenital melanocytic nevi or atypical nevi.
rationales.F06: The dermoscopic features are highly suggestive of a melanocytic lesion, such as a congenital melanocytic nevus or atypical nevus.
rationales.F08: The histopathological features of a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction are consistent with an atypical compound nevus.
rationales.F09: The presence of an atypical nevus with areas of dermal fibrosis suggests a possible congenital melanocytic nevus or atypical nevus.
rationales.F10: The gene expression testing score is consistent with a benign nevus, which rules out more aggressive lesions.
